The satellite is built on Redwire's Hammerhead spacecraft platform.

launches.name: Vikram-I | NILA III & SCOPE
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre First Launch Pad
launches.desc:
Second launch of Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-I launch vehicle. 

2 payloads will be launched on board:
- HEX20 (India)'s NILA III satellite (4U cubesat), which will test OhmSpace (Italy)'s high-temperature resistojet/3D-printed electric propulsion system for high-thrust orbital manoeuvres
- Skyroot's own SCOPE satellite (4U cubesat)

Exolaunch of Germany will provide the cubesat deployer.

launches.name: Falcon Heavy | Griffin Mission One
launches.desc: Demonstration flight of the Astrobotic Griffin lander and its engines, initially contracted for the NASA VIPER (Volatiles Investigating Polar Exploration Rover) mission. The vacated payload spot will now host the FLIP (FLEX Lunar Innovation Platform) lunar rover from Astrolab.

launches.name: H3-30 | IGS Optical Diversification 1
launches.desc: The IGS Optical Diversification 1 is a Japanese optical reconnaissance satellite. The satellite is operated by the Cabinet Satellite Information Center. The satellite serves both Japan's national defense and civil natural disaster monitoring.

launches.desc: Starliner-1 is the first operational flight of a Starliner spacecraft to the International Space Station as part of NASA's Commercial Crew Program. launches.name: KAIROS | JSDF SDA Demonstration satellite

launches.name: Electron | Aspera
launches.loc: Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1, Mahia Peninsula, New Zealand
launches.desc: Aspera houses an ultraviolet telescope and will examine hot gas in the  intergalactic medium, thought to be contributing to the birth of stars and planets. Aspera will be the first NASA astrophysics mission to gather and map these ultraviolet light signatures, potentially unlocking a deeper understanding of the origins of stars, planets, and life in the universe.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 5 | Axiom Space Mission 5
launches.desc: This is a Crew Dragon flight for a private company Axiom Space. The mission will carry a professionally trained commander alongside three private astronauts to and from the International Space Station for a month.
